question.text: The Aztecs, meanwhile, used this language, whose modern variety is still widely spoken today. The words "chipotle" and "axolotl" come from this language.
question.clue: Historians learned to write in this language at schools called calmecacs ("kahl-MAY-kahks").

swap.leadin: In trying to escape from the capital of this empire, Spanish soldiers experienced La Noche Triste [la no-chay tree-stay].
swap.text: Name this empire, led by Montezuma, which was conquered by Hernan Cortes in 1521.
swap.clue: Cuauhtemoc ruled during the decline of this empire, whose demise began after a foreign expedition landed near modern day Veracruz.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the native peoples of the Americas.
question.text: Sites from this Mesoamerican civilization include La Venta and San Lorenzo, which were mysteriously abandoned. They created giant stone heads, thought to be depictions of their rulers.
question.clue: This culture created "elongated man" figurines as well as a greenstone statue of a man holding a were-jaguar ("wair-jaguar").

swap.text: This Mesoamerican culture played the ballgame in remembrance of the mythical Hero Twins, who played it to escape Xibalba ("shee-BAL-bah"). Thirteen ballcourts were built by this culture at its site of Chichen Itza on the Yucatan Peninsula.
swap.clue: A revolt of these people began a fifty-year long Caste War in the second half of the 19th century.

question.leadin: The general Siyaj K'ak' overthrew the king of this city in 378 CE and replaced him with a ruler from Teotihuacan.
question.text: Name this Mayan city in modern-day Guatemala that was home to the Lost World complex. This city fought a series of wars with the rival city of Calakmul.
question.clue: This polity's rival was called the Snake Kingdom, and this polity's namesake hiatus began after its ruler Wak Chan K'awiil was defeated by this polity's rival and Caracol.

swap.text: This site, located in the Yucatan Peninsula in present day Mexico, is the site of a step pyramid known as the Temple of Kukulcan. This site contains an observatory referred to as El Caracol, and a Mayan ball game court.
swap.clue: This location was once part of a league with neighboring Uxmal .

question.text: Under the presidency of Efrain Rios Montt, the Guatemalan government committed a genocide against these peoples, killing almost 40% of them. One of these people won the 1992 Nobel Peace Prize for her autobiography.
question.answerHtml: Maya peoples [accept K’iche’; accept Q’eqchi’] (The autobiography is I, Rigoberta Menchú.)
question.clue: The modern-day Zapatista Army of National Liberation in Chiapas, inspired by Zapata's agrarian reforms, is majority-run by these peoples. Also in Chiapas is this ethnic group's city of Palenque.

swap.leadin: Excavation of burials in these people's city of La Venta has uncovered numerous jade artifacts.
swap.text: Name this civilization. This ancient Mesoamerican civilization's other sites include San Lorenzo.
swap.clue: Much of their art is based on a jaguar god, including much in that capital, La Venta.

question.text: Seventh century CE rulers of this city adopted the title of "ball player" when they took the throne of this Maya city in modern-day Chiapas.
question.clue: The French explorer Jean-Frederic Waldeck resided for a time at this city, where a leafy corn plant mural is located at its "foliated cross" complex.

swap.leadin: Alfonso Caso established a chronology for this site consisting of five periods, and discovered its extensive "Tomb Seven" shrine.
swap.text: Name this archaeological site. Hundreds of artistic figures found here termed "Danzantes" suggest that the inhabiting civilization practiced human sacrifice.
swap.clue: Another monument depicts men with scrolls in place of their genitalia who likely represent mutilated war captives - that being the Temple of the Danzantes, or the "Building of the Dancers."

question.leadin: Civilizations utilizing this system also used a smaller-scale system with Haab' and Tzolk'in components.
question.text: Identify this primarily base-20 system. The end of a b'ak'tun was predicted by this system's Long Count.
question.clue: The Book of Chilam Balam of Chumayel discusses this system, which was split into the divine Tzolk'in and civil Haab' derived from "Venus rounds."

swap.text: This civilization, whose descendants are still around in Oaxaca, resided in vast cities like Monte Alban and Mitla. They also conquered Tehuantepec after being driven from their greatest cities by the Mixtecs.
swap.clue: The chief god of this culture was the thunder god Cocijo.

question.leadin: The supposedly "Ethiopian" features of these artworks led archaeologist Jose Melgar y Serrano to hypothesize that their makers had originated in Africa.
question.text: Name these artworks that depict men wearing protective helmets, found at sites like San Lorenzo and La Venta.
question.answerHtml: colossal heads [accept synonyms for colossal like large, titanic, enormous; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers like “Olmec heads”; prompt on just heads]

swap.text: The Sun Stone later immortalized in an Octavio Paz poem was designed by this Mesoamerican civilization centered at Tenochtitlan.
swap.clue: Events that precipitated the decline of this empire include the massacre in the Main Temple and La Noche Triste.

question.leadin: This ruler subjugated the Huastec ("WASS-teck") people around 1450.
question.text: Name this tlatoani ("tla-toh-AH-ni") whose reign saw the beginning of a "Flowery War" with the kingdoms of the Tlaxcala ("tlash-KAH-la")-Pueblan valley. This second Aztec emperor succeeded Itzcoatl ("its-co-AT").

swap.leadin: The first expedition of this type was begun by Tlacaelel after a mutual agreement to begin it at a specific time and place.
swap.text: Name this term for battles undergone in Mesoamerica with the aim of capturing prisoners for human sacrifice. They may have been largely ceremonial.
swap.clue: This planned, ritual conflicts that targeted altepetl ("al-teh-peh-tul") and were conducted partly to use prisoners for human sacrifice.

question.leadin: The Tabasco gave him a woman known as Malitzin to be his wife and interpreter.
question.text: Name this man, who won victories at Cholula in 1519 and at Otumba the following year.
question.clue: The Florentine Codex details how this man's subordinate, Pedro de Alvarado, massacred most of the people at a festival in the Templo Mayor, leading to the retaliatory murder of this man's soldiers during La Noche Triste.

swap.text: This third important Olmec city was the westernmost. It is located at the base of the Tuxtla Mountains, and an important artifact that contains one of the oldest surviving Long Count calendars, the Stela C, was found here.
swap.clue: Located near the Tuxtla Mountains in the Papaloapan River plain, what site is often considered to be the third major centre of the Olmec civilization after San Lorenzo and La Venta?

question.text: The Sun Dagger glyph at this 'observatory' in New Mexico marked the position of the Sun during solstices and equinoxes. This 'observatory' containing the Fajada Butte was an important ritual site for the Pueblo people who lived in "great houses" at this 'observatory'.
question.clue: Near this site, Anna Sofaer documented a spiral petroglyph called the Sun Dagger that may track an 18.6-year lunar cycle.

swap.text: This civilization sacked the Mayan city of Teotihuacan. They had their capital at Tula, Hidalgo and faced the nomadic Chichimec people.
swap.clue: It's not Teotihuacan, but the Mexica ("may-SHE"-kah) passed through the ruins of this culture's capital on their way to settling the Valley of Mexico, which inspired the layout of Tenochtitlan and other Aztec cities.
